title: Competing charge density-wave and superconducting states in a quasi-one dimensional two-band electron-phonon model
authors: C. Bourbonnais, A. Ghosh, M. Haguier
abstract: We apply the renormalization group method to examine the interplay between the charge density-wave and superconductivity phases in two quasi-one-dimensional tight-binding electronic bands coupled by the electron-phonon interaction. The electronic and phonon energy scales are embedded in a two-cutoff scaling scheme at finite temperature for the renormalization group flow equations of intra- and inter-band phonon-mediated interactions between electrons. At the one-loop level different regimes of renormalization are derived covering both the adiabatic and antiadiabatic domains for small and large phonon frequencies. Finite temperature phase diagrams as a function of nesting frustration of the electron spectrum are thus obtained. The possibilities for superimposed charge density-wave and superconducting ordered states are given. The emergence of domes of superconductivity resulting from quantum critical reinforcement of Cooper pairing by charge density-wave order fluctuations is found. The impact of the multiband character of the electronic structure on the ordering temperature of superconductivity, quantum criticality, and isotope effect is discussed.
summary: This theoretical work uses the Renormalization Group method to study the competition between CDW and SC states in a two-band, quasi-1D electron-phonon model. It reveals that quantum fluctuations near a quantum critical point can stabilize SC domes, and the multi-band nature is crucial for understanding the superconducting pairing mechanism. The results provide detailed phase diagrams mapping out the interplay between these competing ground states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex competition between charge density-wave (CDW) and superconducting (SC) ordered states in a quasi-one-dimensional system.
main_result: It finds that quantum fluctuations near a quantum critical point can lead to the emergence of superconducting domes, and the multi-band character significantly impacts the superconducting critical temperature and isotope effect.
method: The primary method employed is the Renormalization Group (RG) technique, applied at the one-loop level to analyze the flow of phonon-mediated interactions.
model_or_system: The model is a quasi-one-dimensional, two-band electron-phonon system described by a tight-binding Hamiltonian coupled to lattice vibrations. The analysis uses functional integrals and RG flow equations.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), CDW susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{CDW}}$), and the isotope effect.
important_parameters: Nesting frustration of the electron spectrum, phonon frequency ($\omega_D$), and the ratio of electronic to phonon energy scales (adiabatic vs. antiadiabatic regimes).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative RG methods and assumes the system can be described by a two-band model with electron-phonon coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-band Fermi surfaces, diagrammatic contributions to pairing interactions (CDW and SC), and phase diagrams showing the evolution of susceptibility and $T_c$ near quantum critical points.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the RG framework for phonon-mediated interactions, derives flow equations for coupling constants, analyzes the resulting susceptibilities for both CDW and SC channels, and finally maps out finite-temperature phase diagrams showing the interplay between the two orders.
why_interesting: The study of competing orders (CDW vs. SC) driven by electron-phonon coupling is a canonical problem in strongly correlated electron physics, providing theoretical insights into unconventional superconductivity mechanisms.
